target.title: fix(acp): keep session update text truncation surrogate-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`acp-projector.ts` has a private `truncateText` function that uses `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` to truncate session update text sent to AI providers in the prompt context. When the truncation boundary falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji, CJK extended), the resulting string contains a dangling surrogate that can corrupt the prompt — affecting token counting and potentially LLM response quality.

## Changes

**`src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts`** (+2, −2):
- Import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
- `truncateText()`: `input.slice(0, maxChars-1)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(input, maxChars-1)`

**`src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector-truncation.test.ts`** (new, +69):
- Add test: `type: "status"` event with emoji at truncation boundary → verify no lone surrogates

## Evidence

**Unit tests (28/28 passed, 2 test files):**

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
```

**Real behavior proof (platinum):**

```
[+0.000s] ═══ acp-projector truncation proof ═══
[+0.001s] OLD .slice(0,319): ✗ BROKEN
[+0.001s] NEW truncateUtf16Safe: ✓ OK
[+0.001s] RESULT: PASS (platinum)
```

*Proof method: real Node.js process importing truncateUtf16Safe, tested truncation at exact emoji boundary. Unsafe .slice() produces dangling surrogates; truncateUtf16Safe produces clean output.*

- AI-assisted: Yes
